faq.meta_description: JetScope FAQ for launch readiness, source review, research workbench boundaries, scenario writes, and protected operations.
faq.title: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.question: Is this state a product failure, or is the capability intentionally not enabled?

scope.title: What can JetScope review today?
scope.why: The stated review scope shows which decisions the product can support without overstating its reach.
scope.body: JetScope combines jet-fuel prices, SAF breakeven pressure, EU reserve stress, source quality, saved scenario assumptions, and research signals into one review workflow.

readiness.title: Why can launch readiness be not ready?
readiness.why: Separating configuration gaps from product failures makes the correct recovery action clear.
readiness.body: Launch readiness reports the actual environment. Missing management configuration, disabled AI research, database issues, or degraded source coverage are disclosed as blockers or review items instead of being hidden.

sources.title: How should I read degraded or fallback sources?
sources.why: A degraded source changes where its figures are safe to use and therefore needs review before citation.
sources.body: Source review separates live, proxy, fallback, unavailable, and error states. A degraded source can still be useful, but it should be reviewed before procurement or reporting use.

research.title: Why might the research workbench be disabled?
research.why: Disabled research is not evidence that the market produced no new signal.
research.body: The Research workbench does not pretend that AI analysis is live when the pipeline is disabled or credentials are incomplete. It shows the boundary and the next review actions.

scenarios.title: Can I save scenarios or refresh market data here?
scenarios.why: Protected writes need explicit authorization before a read-only state can be treated as a malfunction.
scenarios.body: Scenario writes and refresh operations are protected. Without the configured management token, localized FAQ pages and review surfaces stay read-only and link back to the primary workspaces.

limitations: These answers describe the current deployment design intent and do not change with live data; use the Admin page for the environment’s actual readiness.
The FAQ does not replace the current states and limitations on the Sources, Research, or Scenarios pages.

tipping_point_report.meta_description: English JetScope report detail for SAF tipping-point evidence, market source confidence, reserve stress, and research posture.
tipping_point_report.title: Tipping-Point Report
tipping_point_report.question: Does this report's economic case still hold?
tipping_point_report.signal_hint: Conclusion first; an unknown signal remains review-required.
tipping_point_report.probability_hint: Maximum probability across spot SAF purchase and long-term offtake.
tipping_point_report.events_hint: Event sample in the current 42-day review window.
tipping_point_report.events_hint_empty: No events in the current review window.
tipping_point_report.thesis_why: The evidence chain shows whether the model can support a decision or must go through source review first.
tipping_point_report.thesis_lead: JetScope treats the tipping point as a convergence of fossil fuel cost, carbon exposure, reserve stress, and SAF pathway spread. The current fossil cost anchor is {price}.
tipping_point_report.thesis_body: The source posture is {status} with {confidence} confidence. If fallback rows are active, the report remains readable but must be reviewed before publication.
tipping_point_report.reserves_why: Reserve weeks set the urgency: the thinner the cover, the shorter the price and policy reaction window.
tipping_point_report.chart_why: The fossil anchor, carbon-adjusted effective cost, and pathway net-cost ranges — the report's economic case sits in those gaps.
tipping_point_report.chart_why_assumed: No live fossil anchor is available; the price gap is for scenario discussion only.
tipping_point_report.decision_why: Translate model output into reviewable operating implications, so probabilities are not read as a yes-or-no recommendation.
tipping_point_report.decision_body: The decision model presents probabilities and threshold evidence rather than a simple yes/no recommendation.
tipping_point_report.research_why: Explains why this report's argument is changing. Signals are reasons, not conclusions.
tipping_point_report.timeline_why: Records when SAF effective cost actually crossed fossil jet, not when the model expected it to.
tipping_point_report.confidence_why: These four checks explain how much weight the conclusion can carry and which evidence is still missing.
tipping_point_report.next_why: The report becomes actionable only when its sources, scenario assumptions, and publication path remain reachable.

figure_methods.fossil_assumed: Report-page assumed fossil-jet constant of 0.657 USD/L, or no citable timestamp is available
figure_methods.effective_fossil: Effective fossil jet = spot fossil jet + carbon-price pressure at the selected blend rate - subsidy (tipping-point model)

tipping_point_report.source_dashboard: Dashboard read model and market status
limitations: The report describes market-wide thresholds, not one airline’s contracts, inventory, or approvals.
Decision probabilities are model outputs, not observed future behaviour.
No events in a thin review window does not mean there is no risk.
